delete.description: Remove a stored value (a whole stored table included), or, with a dotted name, just one field of it. Deleting something that was never set does nothing and is not an error, so it's safe to run every time. The value must be one workflows are allowed to edit (turn on "Let workflows edit this value" when you create it); a value the workflow creates itself is editable automatically.
delete.name: delete

parameters.description: The name this value is stored under, for example cursor. To work with a single field inside a stored object, add a dotted path such as user.email. Letters, digits, and underscores only; each part can't start with a digit.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Where this value lives: the whole workspace (shared by every workflow), or just this workflow.
parameters.name: scope

deleted.description: Whether a stored value was removed.

delete_rows.description: Remove the rows of a table stored in Lodol whose column holds a value, for example every row whose Status is done. To remove the whole table, use Delete a stored value. Deleting from a table that doesn't exist, or where nothing matches, does nothing and is not an error. Text matches ignoring capitals and spaces at either end, and a number matches the same number written as text (42 and "42"). The value must be one workflows are allowed to edit (turn on "Let workflows edit this value" when you create it); a value the workflow creates itself is editable automatically.

find_rows.description: Look up rows in a table stored in Lodol: the rows whose column matches a value (for example the row whose Email is ana@example.com, or the orders whose Total is more than 100), or every row when no column is chosen. The rows can be sorted by a column, and At most keeps only the first of them, for example the 10 newest orders. Returns the rows, the first of them as row, and how many there are; a table that doesn't exist yet has no rows. For rows that must meet more than one condition, follow this step with Filter list. Text matches ignoring capitals and spaces at either end, and a number matches the same number written as text (42 and "42"). Reading is always allowed.

increment.description: Add a number to a counter and get the new total back. Starts the counter at zero the first time. The value must be a number; if it holds something else, like text, the step fails and nothing is added. Safe to run from many workflow runs at once: every increment is counted, with none lost. The value must be one workflows are allowed to edit (turn on "Let workflows edit this value" when you create it); a value the workflow creates itself is editable automatically.

save_row.description: Keep a row in a table stored in Lodol, for example a customer, an order already handled, or a line in a log, with no spreadsheet to set up. With "Update the row with the same" set to a column, the row that already has the same value there (say, the same Email) is updated instead, so each customer appears once; its other columns are kept. The table is created the first time. Safe to run from many workflow runs at once. A stored table holds up to 5,000 rows. Text matches ignoring capitals and spaces at either end, and a number matches the same number written as text (42 and "42"). The value must be one workflows are allowed to edit (turn on "Let workflows edit this value" when you create it); a value the workflow creates itself is editable automatically.

set.description: Save a value under a name so a later step or a future run can read it back, for example a cursor marking how far the workflow has gotten. Overwrites whatever was stored there before; setting a dotted path fills in any missing objects along the way. A list of rows (for example the rows Read a file returns) fills a stored table in one go; a table holds up to 5,000 rows. The value must be one workflows are allowed to edit (turn on "Let workflows edit this value" when you create it); a value the workflow creates itself is editable automatically.
